markdown:
## Why Behavioral Interviews Work

Research from Schmidt and Hunter shows that structured behavioral interviews have a validity coefficient of 0.51 for predicting job performance — compared to 0.38 for unstructured interviews and 0.10 for years of experience.

### The STAR Framework

Behavioral questions ask candidates to describe past situations. Evaluate responses using STAR:

- S ituation: What was the context?
- T ask: What was the candidate's specific responsibility?
- A ction: What did the candidate do? (Not the team — the candidate)
- R esult: What was the outcome? (Quantified where possible)

### 40 Behavioral Questions by Competency

#### Leadership (Questions 1-8)

- "Tell me about a time you led a team through a significant change."
- "Describe a situation where you had to make a difficult decision with incomplete information."
- "Give an example of how you motivated a team member who was underperforming."
- "Tell me about a time you disagreed with your manager. How did you handle it?"
- "Describe the most effective team you have built. What made it work?"
- "Tell me about a time you had to deliver bad news to your team."
- "Give an example of how you developed someone on your team."
- "Describe a situation where you had to lead without formal authority."

#### Problem-Solving (Questions 9-16)

- "Tell me about the most complex problem you solved at work."
- "Describe a time you identified a problem before anyone else noticed."
- "Give an example of how you approached a problem with no obvious solution."
- "Tell me about a time you had to analyze data to make a decision."
- "Describe a situation where your initial approach to a problem failed."
- "Give an example of how you simplified a complex process."
- "Tell me about a time you had to make a trade-off between quality and speed."
- "Describe how you prioritized when everything seemed urgent."

#### Collaboration (Questions 17-24)

- "Tell me about a successful cross-functional project you worked on."
- "Describe a conflict with a colleague and how you resolved it."
- "Give an example of how you built consensus among stakeholders with different priorities."
- "Tell me about a time you had to work with someone whose style was very different from yours."
- "Describe a situation where you had to give difficult feedback to a peer."
- "Give an example of how you contributed to someone else's success."
- "Tell me about a time you had to adjust your communication style for a different audience."
- "Describe how you handled a situation where a team member was not pulling their weight."

#### Adaptability (Questions 25-32)

- "Tell me about a time you had to learn a new skill quickly."
- "Describe a situation where priorities changed suddenly."
- "Give an example of how you handled ambiguity."
- "Tell me about a time you received critical feedback. How did you respond?"
- "Describe a failure and what you learned from it."
- "Tell me about a time you worked outside your comfort zone."
- "Give an example of how you adapted to a new company culture."
- "Describe a situation where you had to change your approach mid-project."

#### Results Orientation (Questions 33-40)

- "Tell me about a goal you set and exceeded."
- "Describe your most significant professional achievement."
- "Give an example of how you improved a metric or KPI."
- "Tell me about a time you delivered results under pressure."
- "Describe a project that had a measurable business impact."
- "Tell me about a time you went above and beyond what was expected."
- "Give an example of how you turned around a failing project."
- "Describe how you balanced multiple competing priorities to deliver results."

### Scoring Rubric

Rate each response on a 1-5 scale:

| Score | Description |
|---|---|
| 1 | No relevant example; vague or hypothetical response |
| 2 | Weak example; limited detail; unclear candidate role |
| 3 | Adequate example; clear STAR structure; reasonable outcome |
| 4 | Strong example; detailed actions; quantified results |
| 5 | Exceptional example; proactive leadership; significant impact; learning applied |

### Implementation Tips

- Select 4-6 questions per interview (not all 40)
- Map questions to role competencies before the interview
- Use the same questions for every candidate in the same role
- Take notes during the interview (do not rely on memory)
- Score immediately after each interview
- Calibrate scores across interviewers before the debrief
